chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

exercises.name: Make the E7 shape
exercises.purpose: Land the 7th-chord shape that opens the 12-bar blues.

params.fingers: middle(2) on A-string 2nd fret, index(1) on G-string 1st fret, rest open
params.strings_played: all six ring (low E, A, D, G, B, high e)

exercises.coaching: E7 is your open E shape, but the G-string finger is lifted so it rings open (don't fret it). Keep your middle finger on the A string, second fret, and add your index finger on the G string, first fret. That open G note is the difference: it leaves the D string open, and that open D is the '7' — the note that makes this sound like the blues instead of plain old E.

exercises.name: One clean down-strum
exercises.purpose: Strum through all six strings without catching.

params.cue: listen for all six strings ringing, especially the open D string (the b7)

exercises.coaching: Hold E7 and strum down across all six strings. Loose wrist. The 7th note wants to get buried, so listen for the open D string — that D is the '7', the bluesy colour. If a string buzzes, press a touch closer to the fret. That ringing E7 is the whole mood.

exercises.name: Your first shuffle feel
exercises.purpose: Feel the lopsided swing that separates blues from a straight strum.

params.feel: swing — long-short, long-short, not even eighths
params.cue: count '1 - la, 2 - la' with the long beat first

exercises.coaching: Same E7, now with a shuffle. Think long-short, long-short: 'one - and, two - and' but the first half is heavier. Set the metronome to 68 and land on the beat, then let the off-beat lean. That lopsided bounce IS the blues groove. Just sit in it.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: Today you learn the sound that started a hundred years of music. One chord — E7 — and you are already playing the blues.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: E7 is open E, but lift the G-string finger so it rings open, and add your index on the G string first fret while your middle stays on the A string second fret. The open D string — left ringing — is the 7, the blues note.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Hold it, strum all six strings down. Loose wrist. Listen for the open D string — that is the 7, the colour. Buzz? Press closer to the metal. That ringing E7 is the whole mood.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex3_intro: Now the shuffle: long-short, long-short. Metronome at 68, land on the beat, let the off-beat lean. That lopsided bounce is the groove. Sit in it.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: If you can hold E7 and strum it clean with a shuffle feel, you are playing the blues. That is the door to the whole style.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: E7 in your hands, shuffle in your wrist. Most people think blues is hard — it starts with one chord. Lesson 2 of the pack adds A7 and you get your first real change.

lesson.title: Blues Pack 1 — The E7 Chord (the sound of the blues)
lesson.one_line_promise: One chord, and you're already playing the blues.
objectives: Form E7 (middle on A 2nd fret, index on G 1st fret, G-string finger lifted so it rings open)
Strum it clean across all six strings
Feel the shuffle (long-short) bounce over a slow metronome
prerequisites: Em, easy C, G, D, Am (core open-chord set)

free_metronome: hold the shuffle tempo (long-short eighth feel)
